auditor.name: brand-evidence-auditor
auditor.user_agent: BrandEvidenceAuditor/1.0 (read-only site audit; respects robots.txt; contact: site owner)

scope.rendering_verification: not performed — no browser engine was used; all pages judged from served HTML

probes.declared_in: sameAs in entity markup on http://demo.example.com/
sameAs in entity markup on http://demo.example.com/
probes.title: Riverbend Cycling Club — members page

external_corroboration.scope_note: Only URLs the site itself declares (sameAs, identifier, rel=me, rel=author, rel=publisher, cross-domain rel=alternate) and the other common form of its own hostname were requested. No search engine, directory or third-party source the site did not name was consulted. No conclusion is drawn from the absence of external references, and no claim is made about how discoverable this brand is on the web at large — the audit has not looked at the web at large.

findings.title: Structured data disagrees with the visible page
findings.impact: A research agent can quote a price, name or availability that the page does not actually show.
findings.mechanism: Structured data is trusted precisely because it is unambiguous. When JSON-LD asserts a price, name or availability that appears nowhere in the visible text, a system reading the markup extracts a fact the page itself does not support — producing a confidently-stated wrong answer rather than a missing one.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/product-blender.html: JSON-LD price does not match the visible page [structured value="999"; visible value(s)="1299"]

evidence_items.observation: JSON-LD price does not match the visible page
evidence_items.measurement: structured value="999"; visible value(s)="1299"

suggested_action.summary: Make price in JSON-LD render from the same source as the visible value on http://demo.example.com/product-blender.html.
implementation: Bind the JSON-LD field to the same data source that renders the visible value, rather than a separate constant or feed.
Add a build/CI assertion that fails when the serialised markup value differs from the rendered value.
Where the markup is intentionally a starting price, use the correct schema field (e.g. lowPrice within AggregateOffer) and reflect that in the visible copy.
suggested_action.why_it_works: The contradiction exists because two sources produce the fact independently; binding them to one source removes the class of error rather than one instance.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch the page, extract the JSON-LD field and the visible value, and confirm they match; re-run the audit.

findings.title: Canonical URLs conflict with page identity
findings.impact: Content is attributed to the wrong URL, or dropped as a duplicate, making a stable citation target impossible.
findings.mechanism: rel=canonical tells a retrieval system which URL *is* this document. When it points off-site, to a dead URL, or collapses pages with materially different content onto one address, the machine either attributes the content to the wrong address or discards the page as a duplicate — so a citation cannot resolve back to it.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/: two pages with materially different content declare the same canonical URL [other page=http://demo.example.com/city-picker.html; shared canonical=http://demo.example.com/; main-text similarity=0.00] | http://demo.example.com/city-picker.html: two pages with materially different content declare the same canonical URL [other page=http://demo.example.com/mismatch.html; shared canonical=http://demo.example.com/; main-text similarity=0.00]

evidence_items.observation: two pages with materially different content declare the same canonical URL
evidence_items.measurement: other page=http://demo.example.com/city-picker.html; shared canonical=http://demo.example.com/; main-text similarity=0.00

evidence_items.observation: two pages with materially different content declare the same canonical URL
evidence_items.measurement: other page=http://demo.example.com/mismatch.html; shared canonical=http://demo.example.com/; main-text similarity=0.00

suggested_action.summary: Point each page's rel=canonical at its own live, preferred URL.
implementation: Set rel=canonical to the page's own absolute HTTPS URL unless it is a genuine duplicate.
Where pages truly duplicate one another, keep the canonical but make the duplicate's content identical, or differentiate the content and give each its own canonical.
Remove canonicals pointing at URLs that do not return 200.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Canonical is the machine's identity assertion for a document; making it self-consistent gives every citable page exactly one resolvable address.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch each affected page, confirm the canonical resolves to a 200 URL that serves the same content, and re-run the audit.

findings.title: The site names its own brand inconsistently
findings.impact: Claims from this site may be attributed to the wrong organisation, or not connected to the brand at all.
findings.mechanism: An entity-resolution step answers 'which organisation is this?' by reconciling the title suffix, og:site_name, Organization/WebSite JSON-LD, the logo alt text and the copyright line. When these disagree in ways that are not simple abbreviations, the entity cannot be pinned to one name, and claims found here may be attributed to a different organisation or merged with a similarly-named one.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/: brand name asserted by og:site_name [value="Zenith Retail" (normalised: "zenith retail")] | http://demo.example.com/: brand name asserted by Organization/WebSite JSON-LD name [value="Apex Commerce Pvt Ltd" (normalised: "apex commerce")] | http://demo.example.com/: brand name asserted by logo alt text [value="Zenith Retail" (normalised: "zenith retail")] | http://demo.example.com/: brand name asserted by copyright line [value="Zenith Retail" (normalised: "zenith retail")]

evidence_items.observation: brand name asserted by og:site_name
evidence_items.measurement: value="Zenith Retail" (normalised: "zenith retail")

evidence_items.observation: brand name asserted by Organization/WebSite JSON-LD name
evidence_items.measurement: value="Apex Commerce Pvt Ltd" (normalised: "apex commerce")

evidence_items.observation: brand name asserted by logo alt text
evidence_items.measurement: value="Zenith Retail" (normalised: "zenith retail")

evidence_items.observation: brand name asserted by copyright line
evidence_items.measurement: value="Zenith Retail" (normalised: "zenith retail")

suggested_action.summary: Publish one canonical brand name and use it identically in every identity surface.
implementation: Choose the canonical legal/trading name and apply it to og:site_name, the Organization JSON-LD `name`, the logo alt text and the copyright line.
Add `alternateName` to the Organization JSON-LD for legitimate variants rather than using them interchangeably.
Add `sameAs` identifiers (official social, Wikipedia/Wikidata, registry listings) so the entity resolves to one node.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Entity resolution reconciles independent name assertions; making them agree and declaring variants explicitly removes the ambiguity instead of leaving it to inference.
suggested_action.verification: Re-run the audit and confirm all name sources normalise to the same value; check the Organization JSON-LD parses and contains sameAs.

findings.title: Content paths are disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt
findings.impact: Pages under the blocked path can never be used as a source by a compliant retrieval agent or search crawler.
findings.mechanism: A compliant retrieval agent obeys robots.txt before fetching. Any URL matched by a Disallow rule is never fetched, so the content behind it cannot be read, quoted or cited regardless of how good it is.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/robots.txt: robots.txt publishes a Disallow rule that matches content URLs [1 discovered content URL(s) matched by rule: Disallow: /guides/] | http://demo.example.com/guides/torque.html: URL is listed in the sitemap but disallowed to our user-agent [matched robots rule: Disallow: /guides/]

evidence_items.observation: robots.txt publishes a Disallow rule that matches content URLs
evidence_items.measurement: 1 discovered content URL(s) matched by rule: Disallow: /guides/

evidence_items.observation: URL is listed in the sitemap but disallowed to our user-agent
evidence_items.measurement: matched robots rule: Disallow: /guides/

suggested_action.summary: Narrow the Disallow rule so it covers only non-content paths and leaves http://demo.example.com/guides/torque.html crawlable.
implementation: Edit robots.txt and replace the broad rule `Disallow: /guides/` with rules scoped to utility paths only (e.g. Disallow: /cart, Disallow: /checkout).
If some agents must be excluded, scope the block to a named User-agent group rather than *.
Re-publish the sitemap so the now-crawlable URLs are listed.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Removing the matching Disallow prefix is the only thing that allows a compliant fetcher to request the URL; every downstream stage depends on that first fetch.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch robots.txt and confirm no Disallow rule prefixes the affected paths, then re-run this audit and confirm MR-001 no longer fires.

findings.title: Internally-linked pages return errors
findings.impact: Discovery paths terminate early, so the pages beyond the broken link are never read, and referred visitors land on errors.
findings.mechanism: A research agent expanding its view of a site follows internal links. Links whose destination returns 4xx/5xx waste the agent's small fetch budget and truncate the part of the site it ever sees; a human arriving from an AI answer hits the same dead end.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/missing-page.html: internally linked destination returns HTTP 404 [linked from: http://demo.example.com/]

evidence_items.observation: internally linked destination returns HTTP 404
evidence_items.measurement: linked from: http://demo.example.com/

suggested_action.summary: Repair or remove the 1 internal link target(s) that return errors.
implementation: For each broken destination, either restore the page or 301-redirect it to the closest surviving equivalent.
Update the anchors on the referring pages so the link graph no longer points at a dead URL.
Add the corrected URLs to the sitemap.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Fetch budgets are small; every dead destination is a fetch the agent spends without gaining any text, and each one prunes a branch of the site from its view.
suggested_action.verification: Request each previously-broken URL and confirm 200 (or a single 301 to a 200); re-run the audit and confirm MR-003 no longer lists them.

findings.title: The site points at external profiles that do not resolve
findings.impact: Corroboration attempts that follow the site's own declared identifiers fail, weakening entity resolution rather than strengthening it.
findings.mechanism: `sameAs` and equivalent profile links are the site's own claim about which external records describe it. A research agent following one to corroborate the brand gets an error instead. The anchor the site offered for entity resolution does not exist, so corroboration fails at the exact point the site invited it.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/profiles/missing.html: an external identifier declared by this site does not resolve [HTTP 404; declared via sameAs in entity markup on http://demo.example.com/]

evidence_items.observation: an external identifier declared by this site does not resolve
evidence_items.measurement: HTTP 404; declared via sameAs in entity markup on http://demo.example.com/

suggested_action.summary: Correct or remove the declared external identifiers that do not resolve.
implementation: Check each URL in the entity markup's `sameAs` array and replace or delete the ones that error.
Keep only identifiers that are stable and that you control or can verify describe this entity.
Where a profile has moved, point `sameAs` at the current canonical URL rather than relying on a redirect.
suggested_action.why_it_works: sameAs is only useful while every entry resolves to a record about the same entity; a dead entry provides no corroboration and casts doubt on the rest of the array.
suggested_action.verification: Request each sameAs URL and confirm a 2xx response, then re-run the audit with external checks enabled.

findings.title: Pages assert current information but expose no date signal
findings.impact: Time-sensitive claims cannot be dated, so they are either ignored or repeated after they become false.
findings.mechanism: A system deciding whether to repeat a time-sensitive fact needs to know when it was last true. Pages that say 'latest', 'current', 'in stock' or name the current year, while carrying no dateModified, no <time datetime>, and no visible date, offer no way to establish freshness — so the claim is either dropped or repeated long after it stops being true.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal [timeliness phrase="latest"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date; volatile commercial claim present] | http://demo.example.com/blog/news-one.html: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal [timeliness phrase="latest"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date] | http://demo.example.com/blog/news-two.html: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal [timeliness phrase="latest"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date] | http://demo.example.com/offers-archive.html: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal [timeliness phrase="current"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date; volatile commercial claim present] | (+1 further affected page(s))

evidence_items.observation: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal
evidence_items.measurement: timeliness phrase="latest"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date; volatile commercial claim present

evidence_items.observation: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal
evidence_items.measurement: timeliness phrase="latest"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date

evidence_items.observation: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal
evidence_items.measurement: timeliness phrase="latest"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date

evidence_items.observation: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal
evidence_items.measurement: timeliness phrase="current"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date; volatile commercial claim present

evidence_items.observation: page asserts current information but exposes no date signal
evidence_items.measurement: timeliness phrase="this week"; no JSON-LD date, no <time datetime>, no parseable visible date

suggested_action.summary: Expose a machine-readable last-updated date on pages that assert current information.
implementation: Add `dateModified` (and `datePublished` where relevant) to the page's JSON-LD, driven by the real edit timestamp.
Render a visible 'Last updated: <date>' line wrapped in <time datetime="YYYY-MM-DD">.
For volatile commercial facts, state the effective date next to the value rather than only in the page footer.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Freshness is established from explicit date assertions; without one, a citing system has no evidence that a current-sounding claim is still valid.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch the page and confirm a parseable date is present in markup and visible text; re-run the audit.

findings.title: Content pages offer no in-content route to the next step
findings.impact: Referred visitors have no route from the answer to the related detail or action, and related pages are not connected for retrieval.
findings.mechanism: A visitor arriving from an AI answer arrives mid-journey with a partly-answered question. If the page body contains no contextual links onward — only global navigation — the visitor must restart their search from the menu, and a system following the site's structure finds no relationship between this page and the pages that complete the answer.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/copy-a.html: substantial content page has no contextual links to a next step [main-region internal links=0 (excluding nav/header/footer); main-region words=183] | http://demo.example.com/copy-b.html: substantial content page has no contextual links to a next step [main-region internal links=0 (excluding nav/header/footer); main-region words=183]

evidence_items.observation: substantial content page has no contextual links to a next step
evidence_items.measurement: main-region internal links=0 (excluding nav/header/footer); main-region words=183

evidence_items.observation: substantial content page has no contextual links to a next step
evidence_items.measurement: main-region internal links=0 (excluding nav/header/footer); main-region words=183

suggested_action.summary: Add contextual in-body links from content pages to the related detail or action page.
implementation: In each content page's body, link to the two or three most related pages using descriptive anchor text.
Place a clear next-step action (pricing, booking, contact, documentation) inside the main content region, not only in the header.
Add a short 'related' block generated from real topical relationships rather than a generic recirculation widget.
suggested_action.why_it_works: It converts the arrival page into a route: the visitor continues without re-searching, and the link graph gains the topical edges retrieval uses to relate pages.
suggested_action.verification: Re-run the audit and confirm affected pages carry three or more main-region internal links.

findings.title: The page never states plainly what it is about
findings.impact: Neither a referred visitor nor a citing system can confirm what this page or entity actually is.
findings.mechanism: A visitor arriving from an AI answer has no browsing context — they did not navigate here, they were sent. If the opening content contains no plain declarative sentence naming the product/organisation and what it does, the visitor cannot confirm they are in the right place, and a citing system has no self-contained sentence to quote as a definition of the entity.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/: the opening content contains no plain statement of what this is [first 77 served words contain no definitional sentence pattern; opening text: "Shop everything at Zenith Retail Welcome. Thousands of products across kitchen, home, tools and outdoor. Free delivery on orders above ₹499. New stock lands ev…"] | http://demo.example.com/product-blender.html: the opening content contains no plain statement of what this is [first 121 served words contain no definitional sentence pattern; opening text: "Vortex 600W blender The Vortex 600W blender costs ₹1,299 and comes with a 1.5 litre jar, a pulse setting and a two year warranty on the motor. The blades are s…"]

evidence_items.observation: the opening content contains no plain statement of what this is
evidence_items.measurement: first 77 served words contain no definitional sentence pattern; opening text: "Shop everything at Zenith Retail Welcome. Thousands of products across kitchen, home, tools and outdoor. Free delivery on orders above ₹499. New stock lands ev…"

evidence_items.observation: the opening content contains no plain statement of what this is
evidence_items.measurement: first 121 served words contain no definitional sentence pattern; opening text: "Vortex 600W blender The Vortex 600W blender costs ₹1,299 and comes with a 1.5 litre jar, a pulse setting and a two year warranty on the motor. The blades are s…"

suggested_action.summary: Open http://demo.example.com/ with one plain sentence stating what it is, who it is for, and what it does.
implementation: Add a lead sentence of the form '<Brand> is a <category> that <does what> for <audience>.' as the first paragraph of the main content.
Follow it with two or three sentences covering the key attributes a stranger would need (coverage, availability, pricing model, location).
Mirror the same sentence in the meta description and in the Organization/Product JSON-LD `description`.
suggested_action.why_it_works: It supplies exactly the self-contained, quotable statement that both a referred visitor and a citing machine need, instead of leaving the definition to be inferred from imagery and slogans.
suggested_action.verification: Re-run the audit and confirm a definitional sentence is detected in the first 120 served words.

findings.title: Content pages carry a noindex directive
findings.impact: The page is excluded from indexes that many retrieval pipelines query, so systems answering from an index cannot cite its facts.
findings.mechanism: A `noindex` in a meta robots tag or the X-Robots-Tag header tells indexers to drop the page from their corpus. Systems that answer from a pre-built index cannot surface it, and agents that fetch live typically treat the same directive as an exclusion signal.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/offers-archive.html: page excludes itself from indexing via meta robots tag [meta robots tag value: noindex, follow]

evidence_items.observation: page excludes itself from indexing via meta robots tag
evidence_items.measurement: meta robots tag value: noindex, follow

suggested_action.summary: Remove the noindex directive from http://demo.example.com/offers-archive.html and keep it only on genuine utility URLs.
implementation: Delete the `noindex` value from the meta robots tag (or the X-Robots-Tag header) on the affected templates.
If the intent was to suppress duplicates, use rel=canonical to the preferred URL instead — canonicalisation consolidates without removing the page from the corpus.
Confirm no CDN/edge rule re-adds X-Robots-Tag for these paths.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Indexers treat noindex as an instruction to discard the document entirely; canonicalisation expresses duplicate intent without erasing the page.
suggested_action.verification: Request the URL and confirm no `noindex` in either the HTML head or the X-Robots-Tag header; re-run the audit.

findings.title: Pages are not distinguishable by title or heading
findings.impact: The wrong page can be selected as the source for a claim, and citations cannot be labelled meaningfully.
findings.mechanism: Titles and H1s are the primary labels a retrieval system uses to tell one document from another and to decide which page answers a query. When several distinct URLs share one title, or a page has no title or no H1, the retrieval layer cannot tell the pages apart and may select or cite the wrong one.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/mismatch.html: distinct pages with different content publish an identical title [title="Wholesale fasteners — Zenith Retail" also used by http://demo.example.com/promo-heavy.html; main-text similarity=0.00; 2 URLs share it]

evidence_items.observation: distinct pages with different content publish an identical title
evidence_items.measurement: title="Wholesale fasteners — Zenith Retail" also used by http://demo.example.com/promo-heavy.html; main-text similarity=0.00; 2 URLs share it

suggested_action.summary: Give every distinct page a unique title and a single descriptive H1.
implementation: Template titles as `<specific page subject> — <brand>` so the subject appears before the brand.
Ensure exactly one H1 per page containing the page subject in plain words.
Where pages legitimately duplicate, consolidate them with rel=canonical instead of leaving both indexable.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Selection and citation labelling operate on title/H1; unique, subject-first labels let the retrieval layer choose and name the right document.
suggested_action.verification: Re-run the audit and confirm no duplicate titles remain across sampled URLs.

findings.title: Primary content is absent from the served HTML
findings.impact: A fetcher that does not execute JavaScript obtains no substantive text from the page and cannot quote or cite anything on it.
findings.mechanism: Many retrieval fetchers read only the HTML the server returns and do not execute JavaScript. When the served document is an empty application shell, the page is complete to a human browser and effectively blank to the machine, so there is no text to extract or quote.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/app-shell.html: served HTML contains almost no main-region text; content appears to be assembled client-side [main-region words in served HTML=0 (threshold 120); empty application root element id="root"] | http://demo.example.com/catalog.html: served HTML contains almost no main-region text; content appears to be assembled client-side [main-region words in served HTML=0 (threshold 120); empty application root element id="app"]

evidence_items.observation: served HTML contains almost no main-region text; content appears to be assembled client-side
evidence_items.measurement: main-region words in served HTML=0 (threshold 120); empty application root element id="root"

evidence_items.observation: served HTML contains almost no main-region text; content appears to be assembled client-side
evidence_items.measurement: main-region words in served HTML=0 (threshold 120); empty application root element id="app"

suggested_action.summary: Server-render or pre-render the primary content of http://demo.example.com/app-shell.html so the served HTML contains the page's key facts as text.
implementation: Enable server-side rendering or static pre-rendering for the affected templates so the first HTML response contains headings, body copy and key attributes.
Where full SSR is impractical, inline a machine-readable summary of the page's key facts (name, what it is, key attributes, price/availability) into the served HTML.
Keep the rendered text identical to what the client-side app displays so the two never disagree.
suggested_action.why_it_works: The extraction stage operates on the served bytes; putting the facts in those bytes is the only change that makes them retrievable without a browser engine.
suggested_action.verification: Run `curl -s <url> | wc -w` (or re-run this audit) and confirm the served HTML contains the page's key sentences.

findings.title: The same content is served at multiple URLs without consolidation
findings.impact: Citation targets fragment across addresses and duplicate copies can be mistaken for independent sources.
findings.mechanism: When near-identical content exists at several self-canonical URLs, a citing system has no basis for choosing which address represents it. Citations then split across addresses, and the same fact appearing at multiple URLs can look like independent corroboration when it is one source repeated.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/copy-a.html: a second URL serves near-identical content without consolidation [duplicate of http://demo.example.com/copy-b.html; main-text similarity=1.00; canonicals: http://demo.example.com/copy-a.html vs http://demo.example.com/copy-b.html]

evidence_items.observation: a second URL serves near-identical content without consolidation
evidence_items.measurement: duplicate of http://demo.example.com/copy-b.html; main-text similarity=1.00; canonicals: http://demo.example.com/copy-a.html vs http://demo.example.com/copy-b.html

suggested_action.summary: Consolidate the duplicate URLs onto one canonical address.
implementation: Pick the preferred URL for each duplicate cluster and set rel=canonical on the others to point at it.
Where the duplicates serve no purpose, 301-redirect them instead of keeping both live.
Ensure internal links and the sitemap reference only the preferred URL.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Consolidation gives the content one resolvable identity, so citation and corroboration signals accumulate on a single address.
suggested_action.verification: Confirm the non-preferred URLs canonicalise or redirect to the preferred one, then re-run the audit.

findings.title: A declared external profile does not mention the brand name
findings.impact: The site's declared corroboration does not corroborate it, so cross-source entity resolution may attach the wrong external record.
findings.mechanism: An identifier only corroborates an entity if the destination is recognisably about that entity. When a declared profile resolves but its title, site name and visible text never contain any form of the brand name, an agent following the link to confirm the entity finds no confirmation — and, worse, may attach the wrong external record to the brand.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/profiles/unrelated.html: a declared external identifier resolves but does not name this brand [retrieved title="Riverbend Cycling Club — members page"; no compatible form of "Zenith Retail", "Apex Commerce Pvt Ltd" found in its title, site name, visible text or URL path]

evidence_items.observation: a declared external identifier resolves but does not name this brand
evidence_items.measurement: retrieved title="Riverbend Cycling Club — members page"; no compatible form of "Zenith Retail", "Apex Commerce Pvt Ltd" found in its title, site name, visible text or URL path

suggested_action.summary: Point declared identifiers at profiles that name the brand, and state the brand name on those profiles.
implementation: Review each sameAs destination and confirm the profile's own title or description contains the canonical brand name.
Where the profile is correct but does not name the brand, update the profile's display name or description on that platform.
Remove identifiers for records that describe a different entity, such as a parent company or an individual founder, unless that relationship is stated explicitly in the markup.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Cross-source entity resolution works by finding the same name asserted in independent places; a profile that never states the name cannot supply that agreement.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch each sameAs URL and confirm the brand name appears in its title or description; re-run the audit with external checks enabled.

findings.title: Substantive content depends on a user context the fetcher cannot supply
findings.impact: A context-free agent retrieves incomplete or unrepresentative information and cannot know which context the answer applies to.
findings.mechanism: When the page's real content only appears after a location, store, city or postcode is chosen, a context-free fetcher receives the pre-selection state. It then reads either nothing or an arbitrary default, so what it extracts may not correspond to any answer a real user would receive — and it has no basis for choosing a context.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/city-picker.html: page content appears to depend on a user context the fetcher cannot supply [context control found: "Select your city to see delivery slots and stock."; served main-region words=22]

evidence_items.observation: page content appears to depend on a user context the fetcher cannot supply
evidence_items.measurement: context control found: "Select your city to see delivery slots and stock."; served main-region words=22

suggested_action.summary: Serve a crawlable, context-independent default view alongside the personalised one.
implementation: Render a default (e.g. national or flagship-location) version of the content in the served HTML, with the personalised view layered on top after selection.
State explicitly in text which context the default represents ('Prices shown for <default region>; availability varies by location').
Expose per-context pages at stable URLs (e.g. /delivery/mumbai) and list them in the sitemap so each context is separately citable.
suggested_action.why_it_works: It gives the context-free reader something true and attributable to extract, and gives each real context its own stable address rather than hiding all of them behind one interactive state.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch the page without cookies or location headers and confirm substantive content and an explicit context statement are present; re-run the audit.

findings.title: Promotional and repeated blocks crowd out the page's substance
findings.impact: Extraction returns promotional copy rather than the page's substantive facts, and referred visitors must search the page for the answer.
findings.mechanism: Promotional modules and repeated blocks are hard for an extractor to separate from content and they occupy the first screen for a visitor. When they account for a large share of the page's text, the extracted content is mostly offers rather than facts about the subject, and the referred visitor has to hunt for the answer they were sent to find.
findings.evidence: http://demo.example.com/promo-heavy.html: an identical text block is emitted several times on the same page [block repeated 3× : "Members save an extra five percent on every order this week"; promotional share of main text=21%]

evidence_items.observation: an identical text block is emitted several times on the same page
evidence_items.measurement: block repeated 3× : "Members save an extra five percent on every order this week"; promotional share of main text=21%

suggested_action.summary: Reduce promotional share above the fold and de-duplicate repeated blocks.
implementation: Move promotional modules below the page's primary explanatory content in the DOM order.
Mark promotional containers with `aside` (or `role="complementary"`) so extractors can separate them from the main content.
Render repeated modules once and reference them, instead of emitting the same block multiple times.
suggested_action.why_it_works: Extractors keep main-region text and drop complementary regions; DOM order and region semantics decide what survives, and repetition dilutes the page's distinctive text.
suggested_action.verification: Re-run the audit and confirm promotional share of main-region text falls below 25%.

proactive_opportunities.title: Let crawlers see what actually changed (accurate sitemap lastmod)
proactive_opportunities.observation: A sitemap was retrieved listing 13 URL(s) but only 0 <lastmod> value(s).

suggested_action.summary: Emit an accurate <lastmod> for every sitemap entry, driven by the content's edit time.
implementation: Generate lastmod from the content management system's modified timestamp, not the build time, so unchanged pages keep their original date.
Regenerate the sitemap on publish rather than on a fixed schedule.
suggested_action.why_it_works: lastmod is the cheapest freshness signal a crawler can read before spending a fetch; accurate values get changed pages re-read sooner and stop unchanged pages consuming the budget.
suggested_action.verification: Fetch the sitemap and confirm lastmod values differ across pages and match recent edits.

limitations: Partial audit: fewer pages were read than requested, so shares and breadth are measured over a small sample. Findings remain valid for the pages named.

The audit reads served HTML only and does not execute JavaScript. Pages whose content is assembled client-side are reported as what a non-rendering fetcher observes; the rendered state was not performed — no browser engine was used; all pages judged from served HTML.

Off-site corroboration is limited to the external identifiers the site itself declares. No search engine or directory was consulted, no claim is made about whether any AI product uses this site, and the absence of external references is never treated as a defect.
13 page(s) were sampled under a 20-page / 60s budget; findings describe the sample, and shares are reported relative to it.
1 URL(s) were not fetched because robots.txt disallows them; they are reported as findings, not inspected.
